Stage 3 · Grammar

Grammar

I've got a phone · She's got a car
FormExample
I / you / we / they → 've gotI've got a phone.
he / she / it → 's gotShe's got a car.
Have you got …?Have you got a pen? — Yes, I have.
  • I / you / we / they → 've got (have got): I've got a phone.
  • he / she / it → 's got (has got): She's got a car.
  • Question: Have you got…? Short answer: Yes, I have / No, I haven't.
  • 've got = a thing you own. Ask a friend: Have you got a pen?

→ Present Simple (I work / she works) comes later.

🔧 Build it yourself
  • 🔧 Build it yourself
  • Build it: I have got → I'VE got a phone. Question: HAVE you got a pen?
  • ⚠ У меня есть… / Менде … бар = I've got… — English uses a verb, not 'at me is'.

Stage 6 · Speaking

Your turn

Write two short lines: what you've got, and ask a question.

When you finish, open the model answer and check yourself.

Model answer

I've got a phone and a book in my bag. I haven't got a laptop. Have you got a pen?

Check yourself:

  • Did you use I've got …?
  • Did you use has got ('s got) for he / she?
  • Did you ask Have you got …?
Talk to Sam. Answer with the words from this lesson.

Read each message. Tap 🔊 to hear Sam.

Sam

Hi again! I'm Sam. 👋

Sam

What's in your bag?

Sam

Nice! 📱

Sam

Have you got a laptop?

Sam

Cool! 💻

Sam

Listen: “She have got a car.” 🤔

Why

he / she / it → has got ('s got): She's got a car. I / you / we / they → have got.

Sam

Yes! “She's got a car.” Great catch. 🌟

Feedback

Well done: you said what you've got and fixed has / have. Next time, say it out loud too.
